skills.name: Kitchen planning and the work triangle

worked_example.problem: The sink is {a} m from the cooker, the cooker {b} m from the fridge, and the fridge {c} m from the sink. How long is the work triangle? Is it well planned?
steps: Each side is between {sideMin()} m and {sideMax()} m.
The total is between {totalMin()} m and {totalMax()} m.

cards.idea: A kitchen has three work centres: storage (fridge), preparation and cleaning (sink), and cooking (cooker).
example: Vegetables come from the fridge, are washed at the sink, and are cooked on the cooker.

cards.idea: The work triangle joins the sink, the cooker and the fridge. Add its three sides to find its total length.
example: {a} m + {b} m + {c} m = {triangleTotal(a, b, c)} m.

cards.idea: A good work triangle: each side {sideMin()} m to {sideMax()} m, and a total of {totalMin()} m to {totalMax()} m.
example: Too long: too much walking. Too short: the cook has no room to work.

check.prompt: Why should the work triangle not be too long?

right.text: The cook would walk too much and waste time and energy.

wrong.text: The fridge would get too cold.
wrong.explain: The length of the triangle does not change the fridge.
A long triangle only means more walking.
The sink works anywhere; the problem is the walking.

wrong.text: The kitchen would look too small.
wrong.explain: The problem is wasted walking, not looks.

questions.prompt: How long is this work triangle altogether?

misconceptions.explain: Add all three sides: sink–cooker, cooker–fridge and fridge–sink.

pick.why: The sink: washing vegetables and plates.
The cooker: boiling rice and frying fish.
The fridge: keeping milk and meat cold.
The sink: peeling cassava before cooking.
The fridge: storing leftover soup safely.

questions.prompt: Where in the kitchen should you do this: {x.t}?

misconceptions.explain: That is a different work centre.

questions.prompt: Is this work triangle well planned? (Each side {sideMin()} m to {sideMax()} m; total {totalMin()} m to {totalMax()} m.)

distractors.text: a side is too long: too much walking
a side is too short: the work centres are crowded
the total is too long: too much walking
the total is too short: the work centres are crowded

misconceptions.explain: Check each side first, then add them: total {triangleTotal(a, b, c)} m.

solution: Sides: {a} m, {b} m, {c} m. Total: {triangleTotal(a, b, c)} m.

right.text: Store food covered and in the right place.
Turn off the cooker as soon as the food is ready.

wrong.text: Leave the washing-up until the next day.
wrong.explain: Dirty dishes attract flies and take longer to clean later.
Planning saves money and avoids waste.

wrong.text: Leave the gas on low all day.
wrong.explain: That wastes gas and is dangerous.

wrong.text: Put a table in the middle of the work triangle.
wrong.explain: Nothing should block the work triangle.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: The work triangle joins the sink, the cooker and the fridge.
A very long work triangle means too much walking.
Cleaning as you go keeps the kitchen tidy.
The sink is the cleaning centre.

wrong.text: The fridge is the cooking centre.
wrong.explain: The fridge is the storage centre; the cooker is the cooking centre.

wrong.text: A cupboard in the middle of the work triangle makes work easier.
wrong.explain: Nothing should block the work triangle.

wrong.text: A work triangle should be as long as possible.
wrong.explain: Too long means too much walking: each side about 1.2 m to 2.7 m.
